Weil Sentences: A2 Word Order Exercises

Study four German examples with English meanings, then try four questions and check the explained answers.

A2 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the rule

Weil introduces a reason clause and sends the conjugated verb to the end of that clause. The main clause retains normal word order, while the subordinate clause follows its own verb-final pattern.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not write weil ich bin müde in standard written German; use weil ich müde bin.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich lerne Deutsch, weil ich in Deutschland arbeiten möchte.I learn German because I want to work in Germany.
Worked example 2Sie bleibt zu Hause, weil sie krank ist.She stays home because she is ill.
Worked example 3Wir gehen früh, weil der Bus um sieben Uhr kommt.We leave early because the bus arrives at seven.
Worked example 4Er isst, weil er Hunger hat.He eats because he is hungry.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Complete each reason clause with the present-tense form of the verb in brackets. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich komme nicht, weil ich krank ___. (sein)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: bin

Verb-final after weil.

Question 2. Sie lernt, weil sie morgen eine Prüfung ___. (haben)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: hat

The finite verb ends the subordinate clause.

Question 3. Wir bleiben hier, weil es ___. (regnen)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: regnet

Finite verb at the end.

Question 4. Er geht schlafen, weil er müde ___. (sein)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: ist

Sein comes at the end of the weil-clause.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
